title: Book a clinic appointment from a plain sentence
customerProblem: Staff manually pick dates, times, and rooms in the scheduler, which is slow and error-prone.
shortDescription: Type or speak a request like 'Dr. Rao on Thursday at 3 in Room 2' and the appointment is created on the Scheduler with one confirmation tap.
controlFeatures: Appointment CRUD, resource rooms, quick appointment add
workflowSummary: Enter request, preview the parsed appointment, confirm, see it placed on the month view.
aiOperation: Convert a natural-language request into structured appointment data (title, start, end, resource) and add it to the Scheduler.

details.customerProblem: Manual appointment entry is slow and mistakes in time or room are common.
details.featuresEnhanced: Quick appointment add, resources, month view
details.customerInput: A short sentence describing the appointment.
details.aiOperation: Parse the sentence into appointment fields.
details.structuredOutput: JSON with title, start, end, resource name, notes.
details.applicationToControl: The parsed fields populate a Scheduler Appointment and are added via AddAppointment.
details.expectedInteraction: User reviews the pre-filled appointment card, edits if needed, confirms; the appointment appears on the calendar.
details.whyAiIsUseful: Parsing varied natural phrasing into exact time/resource data is impractical to hand-code.
details.whyControlIsEssential: The Scheduler's appointment model, resources, and month view are the whole point; the parsed data must map to real Scheduler APIs.
details.labelReplacementAnswer: No. A plain text view cannot store, reschedule, or show conflicts for appointments.
details.minimalSampleWorkflow: One screen with input, preview card, and month view; confirm adds the appointment.

title: Filter the sales grid the way you would say it
targetCustomer: Field sales managers reviewing regional data
customerProblem: Applying filter and sort combinations in a large DataGrid takes several taps and trial and error.
shortDescription: Say 'show top accounts by revenue in the North region' and the DataGrid applies matching filter, sort, and group descriptors.
keywords: datagrid, filter, sort, group, natural language
workflowSummary: Enter instruction, see the generated descriptors, apply, review the filtered grid.
aiOperation: Translate a natural-language instruction into DataGrid filter, sort, and group descriptors.

details.customerProblem: Building multi-condition filters and sorts by hand is tedious and inconsistent.
details.customerInput: A sentence describing the desired view of the grid.
details.aiOperation: Map words to column-level descriptor values.
details.structuredOutput: JSON arrays of filter, sort, and group descriptor objects with column, operator, value, and direction.
details.applicationToControl: Descriptors are instantiated and assigned to DataGrid.FilterDescriptors, SortDescriptors, GroupDescriptors.
details.expectedInteraction: User previews the descriptor summary, taps apply, the grid updates; they can remove any descriptor chip to undo.
details.whyAiIsUseful: Converting free phrasing into precise column/operator/value tuples is a natural language task.
details.whyControlIsEssential: The value is the DataGrid's descriptor-driven filtering, sorting, and grouping; nothing works if the grid cannot consume structured descriptors.
details.labelReplacementAnswer: No. A Label or list cannot filter, sort, or group tabular data.
details.minimalSampleWorkflow: One screen: instruction input, descriptor preview, DataGrid with apply/clear.

title: Field service dispatch board with AI-assisted scheduling
customerProblem: Supervisors juggle service requests, technician availability, and a monthly calendar, often re-entering the same data.
shortDescription: A dispatch workflow where a supervisor reviews incoming requests, uses AI to suggest appointment placement for each technician, and confirms onto the Scheduler.
workflowSummary: List of incoming requests; tap one; AI suggests technician + time slot; confirm; appointment lands on the technician resource row; drag to fine-tune.
aiOperation: Suggest appointment placement (technician, start, duration) for a service request.

details.desiredOutcome: Every request is placed on a technician's week in under a minute with minimal rework.
details.practicalWorkflow: Request list (TabView) -> request detail -> AI suggestion card -> confirm/correct -> appointment on Scheduler -> adjust by drag.
details.pages: Dispatch list, request detail, technician schedule
details.customerBenefit: Faster dispatch, fewer double-bookings, less data re-entry.
details.customerInput: The service request text plus technician availability summary.
details.aiOperation: Rank technicians and propose start time and duration for the request.
details.structuredAiOutput: JSON with technician id, start, end, confidence notes.
details.howOutputDrivesControls: The suggested fields create a Scheduler appointment on the chosen technician resource; the user can still drag it before confirming.
details.userReviewAndCorrection: Suggestion shows as a pre-filled, editable card before it touches the calendar.
details.invalidResponseHandling: If parsing fails or no technician matches, show the error and fall back to manual placement.
details.retryOrFallback: Retry button; manual placement always available on the Scheduler.
details.whyAiAddsCustomerValue: Matching skills, load, and time windows across technicians is exactly the kind of messy judgment AI handles well.
details.whyControlsRemainEssential: The Scheduler resources and drag-to-adjust are the actual scheduling tool; the list and tabs structure the workflow.

title: Inventory reorder dashboard with AI chart suggestions
customerProblem: Managers must decide which chart views best expose stock risk, and rebuilding charts every week wastes time.
shortDescription: A reorder workflow where the manager loads stock data, asks the AI to pick chart series and highlights for stock-risk analysis, and applies the suggestion to the Charts control.
workflowSummary: Load stock list -> ask 'highlight items near reorder point' -> AI proposes series + annotations -> apply -> chart updates -> export summary view.
aiOperation: Analyze the selected dataset and configure chart series, axes, and annotations that surface stock risk.

details.desiredOutcome: A manager gets a meaningful stock-risk chart in seconds instead of manual series tweaking.
details.practicalWorkflow: Stock list (DropDownList filters) -> analysis request -> suggested chart config preview -> apply to Charts -> review annotated chart.
details.customerBenefit: Faster, more consistent stock-risk review; less manual charting.
details.customerInput: The chosen stock dataset plus a short analysis intent.
details.aiOperation: Select series types, fields, thresholds, and annotation values.
details.structuredAiOutput: JSON describing series, axis ranges, and annotation items.
details.howOutputDrivesControls: The JSON is applied to the SfChart series collection and annotations; the RangeSlider scrubs the review period.
details.userReviewAndCorrection: Config preview lists what will change; apply is explicit.
details.invalidResponseHandling: Unparseable suggestions are discarded with a message; the previous chart stays untouched.
details.retryOrFallback: Retry, or fall back to the default stock chart configuration.
details.whyAiAddsCustomerValue: Choosing the right visual encoding for a new question is a judgment call; the manager states intent instead of series types.
details.whyControlsRemainEssential: The Charts control renders, annotates, and lets the manager scrub data; AI only produces the configuration.

title: Clinic patient appointment scheduling without AI
customerProblem: Staff book, reschedule, and cancel appointments across several doctor calendars with no unified mobile view.
shortDescription: A practical booking workflow: search patients, pick doctor and slot on the month view, create or move the appointment, and keep a daily list.
controlFeatures: Appointment CRUD, month view, quick add
workflowSummary: Daily list of appointments -> open month view -> tap slot -> create/reschedule -> daily list updates.

details.desiredOutcome: Front desk can manage all doctor appointments from one mobile screen.
details.practicalWorkflow: Daily ListView of today's appointments; month Scheduler for booking; tap-and-drag to reschedule; confirm dialog on conflicts.
details.customerBenefit: One mobile reference for booking; fewer phone calls back and forth.
details.whyControlsAreEssential: The Scheduler's month view, appointment model, and quick add are the core of the workflow; the Calendar gives date context.
details.implementationScope: Two screens, local sample patient/doctor data, appointment CRUD, basic conflict dialog.

title: Expense tracker with grouped, filtered reports without AI
customerProblem: Freelancers track spending in spreadsheets and still cannot answer 'what did I spend on travel last quarter, by week?'
shortDescription: Log expenses, then explore them in a DataGrid grouped by category and week with filter and sort, plus a totals footer.
workflowSummary: Add expense form -> DataGrid grouped by category -> filter by period -> sort by amount -> totals footer.

details.desiredOutcome: Answer period and category questions about spending without leaving the app.
details.practicalWorkflow: Add expense (amount, category, date) -> grid grouped by category with expand/collapse -> DropDownList filters -> sort -> footer totals.
details.customerBenefit: Consistent, repeatable self-reporting; no spreadsheet switching.
details.whyControlsAreEssential: Grouping, filtering, and sorting on live data is precisely what the DataGrid demonstrates; plain lists cannot express grouped totals.
details.implementationScope: Two screens, local sample expense data, CRUD, group/filter/sort, computed footer.

title: Payroll and staff grid use case
customerProblem: HR staff maintain staff and payroll lists that are hard to search, filter, and sort on a laptop spreadsheet while walking the floor.
shortDescription: A staff/payroll workflow built around a DataGrid: searchable staff list, column-level filters, sort, and a detail panel for the selected row.
workflowSummary: Staff tab with DataGrid -> select a row -> detail panel with pay history -> filter by department -> sort by salary -> next run date on Calendar.

details.desiredOutcome: One mobile reference for staff and payroll with fast filtering.
details.practicalWorkflow: TabView (Staff / Payruns) -> DataGrid with selection -> detail panel -> department filter -> salary sort -> payrun dates on Calendar.
details.pages: Staff grid, staff detail, payrun list
details.customerBenefit: Floor-ready payroll reference; answers 'who, when, how much' in two taps.
details.whyControlsAreEssential: Row selection, paging, and descriptor-driven filters are the heart of the workflow and a strong DataGrid showcase.
details.implementationScope: Three screens, local sample staff data, selection detail, filters, sort, payrun list.

title: Retail store operations UI Kit
targetCustomer: Retail franchise owners building a store management app
customerProblem: Small retail teams want consistent mobile screens for daily operations but lack a starting point they can adapt.
shortDescription: A connected UI Kit of store operations screens: today overview, product stock list, reorder form, supplier list, and a stock trend chart.
controlFeatures: DataGrid filters, Chart series, tab navigation
keywords: ui kit, retail, stock, suppliers, store
workflowSummary: Today overview -> product grid -> reorder form -> supplier list -> stock chart; every screen reachable from the others.
screenNames: Today Overview, Product Stock, Reorder Entry, Suppliers, Stock Trend

details.customerNeed: A set of connected, reusable mobile screens for store operations that customers can re-skin with their own data.
details.description: Five screens sharing one retail domain, one visual language, and one navigation pattern.

screens.name: Today Overview
screens.purpose: KPI tiles and top tasks for the day

screens.name: Product Stock
screens.purpose: Filterable product DataGrid with stock levels

screens.name: Reorder Entry
screens.purpose: Form to raise a reorder against a supplier

screens.name: Suppliers
screens.purpose: Supplier list with contact and lead time

details.navigationFlow: Overview links to Stock and Trend; Stock row opens Reorder Entry; Reorder Entry picks from Suppliers; every screen has a back path to Overview.
details.relevantFeatures: Grid filters, chart line series, tab switching, inline toasts
details.customerReuseValue: Screens are data-agnostic; customers bind their own models to the same layouts and flows.

title: Field service crew UI Kit
targetCustomer: Companies building a mobile app for their service crews
customerProblem: Crew apps are rebuilt from scratch every time; teams want proven screens for jobs, parts, and visits.
shortDescription: A connected UI Kit: today's jobs list, job detail with checklist, parts lookup, visit map, and a daily summary.
controlFeatures: ListView templates, map pin overlay, checkbox groups
keywords: ui kit, field service, jobs, parts, map
workflowSummary: Today's jobs -> job detail checklist -> parts lookup -> visit map -> daily summary; all screens connected by the job context.
screenNames: Today's Jobs, Job Detail, Parts Lookup, Visit Map, Daily Summary

details.customerNeed: Ready, connected screens for a field service crew app that customers can adapt to their ticketing data.
details.description: Five screens driven by one job context, with a clear back-and-forth flow.

screens.name: Today's Jobs
screens.purpose: Prioritized job cards for the day

screens.name: Job Detail
screens.purpose: Checklist and notes for one job

screens.name: Parts Lookup
screens.purpose: Searchable parts list with stock counts

screens.name: Visit Map
screens.purpose: Map with pinned stops for the route

screens.name: Daily Summary
screens.purpose: Completed jobs, hours, and parts used

details.navigationFlow: Jobs -> Job Detail (checklist + parts link) -> Parts Lookup; Map shows the route; Summary reachable from Jobs; every screen backs to Jobs.
details.relevantFeatures: Template items, pin overlay, checkable groups
details.customerReuseValue: Job-centric layout and flows transfer to any service domain; customers swap data models only.

title: Warehouse stock count workflow without AI
customerProblem: Cycle counts happen on paper sheets that must later be typed into the system, with frequent transcription errors.
shortDescription: A supervisor walks a zone list, counts items against expected stock, records variance, and reviews a variance summary at the end of the shift.
workflowSummary: Zone list -> item row with expected vs counted -> record variance -> zone completes -> summary gauge shows shift progress.

details.desiredOutcome: Paper-free cycle counts with variance captured at the point of counting.
details.practicalWorkflow: TabView (Zones) -> ListView of items in a zone -> count input per row -> variance flag -> summary screen with RadialGauge progress.
details.pages: Zone list, count screen, shift summary
details.customerBenefit: Counts enter the system the moment they are taken; variance is visible immediately.
details.whyControlsAreEssential: The template-based ListView and progress gauge structure a long, repetitive task; plain forms would not track per-zone progress.
details.implementationScope: Three screens, local sample zone/item data, count entry, variance flag, progress gauge.

title: Teacher gradebook with calendar without AI
customerProblem: Teachers track assignments, grades, and exam dates across separate apps and lose context between them.
shortDescription: A gradebook workflow: a DataGrid of student scores with per-assignment columns, filter by class, and an exam dates Calendar for quick planning.
workflowSummary: Class picker -> DataGrid of scores sorted by student -> select a row for detail -> Calendar showing upcoming exams.

details.desiredOutcome: One place for scores and exam dates, switchable between class and student views.
details.practicalWorkflow: Pick class -> DataGrid with assignment columns -> row selection for a student -> Calendar with exam appointments.
details.pages: Class scores, student detail, exam calendar
details.customerBenefit: Faster mark review and exam planning without app switching.
details.whyControlsAreEssential: Wide tabular data with sorting is a DataGrid strength; the Calendar anchors the exam timeline.
details.implementationScope: Three screens, local sample student/assignment data, sort, selection, calendar appointments.
